description: Give Runner's runCommand a per-command timeout that kills the whole subprocess tree on expiry, and apply it to network-bound git/gh call sites so a hung clone/fetch/push/gh call fails in ~120s with a structured, retry-safe classified result instead of burning the 30-minute work timeout.

tasks.title: Implement the command-timeout primitive in runCommand (timeoutMs, detached group kill, structured result)
tasks.description: Extend CommandResult with optional `status?: "timeout"` and `timeoutMs?: number` fields (absent on normal exit so the object stays byte-identical). Add `timeoutMs?: number` to CommandLineOptions. Inside runCommand, when timeoutMs > 0, layer the existing timeoutSignal(parent, timeoutMs) over the caller signal (reuse, not duplicate — extract/move it to a shared low-level module so system/process.ts can import it without a cycle back into actions/registry.ts, and have registry re-export/re-import to keep core/script behavior identical). Switch spawn to `detached: true` (no unref) so the child leads its own process group; on timeout OR parent-signal abort, group-kill via process.kill(-pid) with a POSIX platform guard (direct child.kill on Windows) and ESRCH/EINVAL fallback. On timeout: resolve with the structured result `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr, status: "timeout", timeoutMs }`, preserving output captured up to the kill and appending the sentinel line `Command timed out after ${timeoutMs/1000}s` to stderr (so the unchanged classifier matches). On parent abort: preserve today's reject behavior. Harden killProcess (process.ts:136) to group-kill a detached child with the same platform guard + fallback, so ACP/runtime/acp-connection.ts and actions/acp/process.ts also reap the group. Omitted/non-positive timeoutMs ⇒ no timer armed, byte-identical result. The primitive MUST NOT encode which commands are timed out.
acceptanceCriteria: runCommand accepts optional timeoutMs via CommandLineOptions; omitted or non-positive ⇒ no timer armed and resolved result is exactly { exitCode, stdout, stderr } (no new keys serialized).

On timeout expiry (driven by fake timer), runCommand kills the child process group and resolves with status === "timeout", timeoutMs recorded, and stdout/stderr captured up to the kill plus the `Command timed out after Ns` sentinel in stderr.
A command that exits (zero or non-zero) before timeoutMs resolves without the timeout category (no status/timeoutMs keys).
A hung direct child is terminated on timeout; a helper subprocess spawned by the child is reaped together with the parent (both PIDs no longer alive, verified via process.kill(pid,0) ESRCH).
killProcess group-kills a detached child (process group signaled, not just the direct PID) with POSIX platform guard and ESRCH/EINVAL fallback.
Work-level AbortSignal abort still terminates the command exactly as before; the per-command timer does not mask or delay the abort, and the abort path rejects (today's behavior).

core/script's with.timeout and mohist/acp-agent's existing timeout behavior are unchanged (they still layer timeoutSignal over context.signal); the single timeoutSignal implementation is shared by core/script, acp, and runCommand.

New spec tests/system-process-timeout.spec.ts covers: omitted/non-positive timeout (byte-identical result), hung direct child killed on timeout, helper subprocess reaped with parent, captured output preserved + sentinel present, killProcess reaps group for detached child, parent-abort path unchanged — all under vi.useFakeTimers() with a real controlled `node -e` child (never real git/gh, never network, never wall-clock).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass; new spec < 500ms.
tasks.output: Modified packages/runner/src/system/process.ts (CommandResult + CommandLineOptions + runCommand + killProcess); extracted/moved timeoutSignal to a shared low-level module with actions/registry.ts re-importing it; new packages/runner/tests/system-process-timeout.spec.ts.
tasks.notes: Per design D1–D5. timeoutSignal currently lives module-private in actions/registry.ts:190 and registry imports from system/process.ts, so importing it back into process.ts would create a cycle — extract it to a shared low-level location (e.g. system/process.ts itself or a new system/timeout-signal.ts) and have registry import from there. Do NOT unref() the detached child — parent still awaits close. SIGTERM matches existing killProcess; SIGKILL-after-grace is explicitly deferred (Open Questions).

tasks.title: Apply the network-command-timeout policy to network git/gh call sites and surface structured retry-safe failures
tasks.description: Add a single exported constant NETWORK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000. Thread `timeoutMs?: number` through GitOptions and have git() forward it into CommandLineOptions.timeoutMs (gh call sites pass it directly via their GhRunner options bag). Apply the network default to every network-bound call site and ONLY those: runtime/workspace.ts (cloneFresh clone, verifyBaseBranch ls-remote, base fetch); actions/push.ts (push, ls-remote probe); actions/rebase.ts (fetch); actions/create-github-pr.ts (push --force-with-lease, fetch base, gh pr list/edit/create); actions/mark-github-pr-ready.ts, actions/merge-github-pr.ts, actions/github-pr-status.ts (network gh calls); actions/github-pr-runtime.ts (gh --version / gh auth status precheck). Leave all local-only commands (rev-parse, status, checkout, diff, merge-base, reset, rebase local/--abort, merge --abort, cherry-pick --abort, cat-file, ls-tree, show-ref, fsck, branch, add, commit, remote get-url) with NO timeoutMs. When a network command's result carries status === "timeout", the delivery action records step name (existing phase label, e.g. git-fetch-base / gh-pr-create / git-push), command summary (existing safe summary, no secrets), and duration (result.timeoutMs) into its existing record()/structured output — no new transport field. Verify the structured timeout output (sentinel `Command timed out after Ns` / `timed out`) is absorbed by the existing retry-safe arm of classifyGhFailure/classifyPushFailure with NO rule additions and NO new GitHubPrErrorCode arm.
acceptanceCriteria: A single NETWORK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS constant (120_000) is the sole source of the network default; no per-command-type budget table exists.
git clone, git ls-remote (base verification), git fetch (base), and git push in workspace.ts + delivery actions are invoked with timeoutMs === NETWORK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS.
gh pr list/edit/create and the gh --version / gh auth status precheck (and other network gh calls) run under the network default timeoutMs.

Local-only git probes (rev-parse, merge-base, status, diff, checkout, reset, rebase local/--abort, add, commit, branch, cat-file, ls-tree, show-ref, fsck, remote get-url) are invoked with timeoutMs === undefined (work-level signal only).

git() threads timeoutMs through GitOptions into CommandLineOptions; GhRunner-typed call sites pass { timeoutMs: NETWORK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS } in the options bag without changing the GhRunner = typeof runCommand seam contract.

When a network command times out, the delivery action surfaces a structured failure carrying the phase step name, a secret-free command summary, and the applied duration; the operator can tell it was a per-command timeout, not a work-level abort.

A network timeout fed to classifyGhFailure / classifyPushFailure classifies as retry-safe and is NOT misclassified as base-moved / protection-conflict / pr-state-conflict / config-error; no new GitHubPrErrorCode arm and no new classification rule is added.

Existing action specs (push.spec.ts, rebase.spec.ts, create-github-pr.spec.ts, github-pr-status.spec.ts, mark-github-pr-ready.spec.ts, merge-github-pr.spec.ts, workspace-prepare*.spec.ts) are extended: the fake GitRunner/GhRunner records options.timeoutMs and asserts network call sites get 120000 and local call sites get undefined; a fake returning a D4-shaped CommandResult ({ status: "timeout", stderr containing "timed out", timeoutMs }) is asserted to produce failureKind: "retry-safe" with the right step/summary/duration. No real network, real git/gh, or wall-clock.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass; specs < 500ms.
tasks.output: Modified packages/runner/src/actions/git.ts (GitOptions + git()), runtime/workspace.ts, actions/push.ts, actions/rebase.ts, actions/create-github-pr.ts, actions/mark-github-pr-ready.ts, actions/merge-github-pr.ts, actions/github-pr-status.ts, actions/github-pr-runtime.ts; new NETWORK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS constant; extended action specs asserting network vs local timeout policy and structured-failure → retry-safe classification.
tasks.notes: Per design D2 (policy lives at call site, not in the primitive) and D4 (step/summary/duration surfaced by delivery actions via existing record()). The action seams (setXxxGitRunnerForTest, setGitHubPrGhRunnerForTest) replace git()/gh() wholesale and sit above runCommand, so they cannot exercise runCommand's internal timeout — the two-layer test split is intentional (D6): primitive proven directly in T-001, policy proven via seams here. Do NOT add with.commandTimeout YAML override (YAGNI, Non-Goal).
